video.title: The Most Overlooked Online Side Hustle Of 2026

summary: Mike describes a local internet presence service for small local businesses, built around better conversion, Google Business Profiles, useful content, landing pages, ads and memorable search phrases. He says AI can now help create content and jingles, while networking remains the main way to find clients. He also shares examples involving pest control, local honey and Nashville party boat bookings, plus several other businesses and income streams. The central lesson is to help a local business get found and make it easy for a potential customer to take the next step.

speakers.name: Mike
speakers.description: Surname not stated; longtime internet marketing and audio business operator.

ideas.name: Local internet presence service for small businesses
ideas.one_liner: Audit and improve how local service businesses get found online and turn visitors into enquiries.
ideas.business_model: Recurring monthly service, with additional one-off work such as jingles.
ideas.customer: Small local service businesses such as plumbers, pest control companies, HVAC firms, roofers, tire stores and painting businesses; especially one- or two-location operators.
ideas.problem: Owners often do not understand online traffic and conversion, neglect their Google Business Profile, publish little useful content and have websites that fail to persuade visitors to call or book.
ideas.offer: Analyse and improve a business's local internet presence through Google Business Profile work, reviews, photos and videos, blog and podcast content, conversion-focused landing pages, Google ads and SER-term jingles.

pricing.model: Monthly retainer plus optional one-off work.

price_points.label: Historical monthly fee for a pest control client

pricing.notes: These prices were described for his earlier pest-control client work; current pricing for the broader service was not stated.

acquisition_channels.details: Attend local networking meetings, build relationships, then arrange one-to-one conversations to show business owners where their online presence is losing potential business.

quote.text: The job of networking is doing one-to- ons with business owners and showing them that this is important
quote.speaker: Mike

acquisition_channels.details: A pest-control podcast and its content brought prospective clients who had listened to Mike explain the work.

quote.text: the podcast gave us a steady flow of customers on autopilot for years and years.
quote.speaker: Mike

acquisition_channels.details: Local one-to-one meetings and client results led to follow-up requests for help.

quote.text: in fact, I got a text just this morning. We're going to we need to do business. I need your help.
quote.speaker: Mike

ideas.delivery: Mike described reviewing and fixing clients' online presence, producing jingles and podcasts, publishing podcast episodes and transcripts as blog posts, and setting up Google ads. Clients supplied recorded audio; he handled the editing and publishing. He says AI can now help write content and jingles, clone a client's voice, and make delivery easier to outsource to a team in the Philippines.
unit_economics_claims: He charged 15 pest-control clients USD 500 per month and charged an additional USD 2,000 for a jingle.
He estimated his monthly time at about one hour per client and said he could bring in USD 2,000 in four hours.

acquisition.how: Mike says finding clients depends on a person regularly attending local networking meetings and having one-to-one conversations. Podcast-led inbound leads can reduce manual prospecting, but are not described as fully automated.

onboarding.how: A person must understand the client's service area, offer and existing online presence. Some content can be generated from prompts and client input.

delivery.how: AI can draft content, clone a voice and generate jingles; publishing and routine production can be outsourced. Review of local facts, ad setup and conversion strategy still need oversight.

billing.how: A recurring retainer can be invoiced automatically, although the transcript does not describe a billing system.

support.how: Mike said he met with clients when they had a problem, so support requires human judgement and availability.

uk_applicability.notes: The model uses local search, websites, reviews, content and paid advertising, which can serve UK local businesses. In-person networking is lawful; any UK outbound email, calls or messaging would need to follow applicable consent and screening rules.

risks: The operator's client results and performance claims are not independently verified.
Winning clients depends heavily on the founder's willingness to network and explain the service.
Client demand can exceed delivery capacity; Mike described clients having more pest-control work than they could staff.
UK outreach must follow PECR rules: avoid unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders without consent, and screen cold calls against TPS and CTPS.

tactics.name: Use one-to-one networking to sell a local presence audit
steps: Attend local business networking meetings regularly.
Ask owners whether they want to grow; Mike says owners who already have all the business they need are not prospects.
Arrange one-to-one conversations with business owners.
Show a concrete issue in their online presence and explain how fixing it could lead to more business.

quote.text: The job of networking is doing one-to- ons with business owners and showing them that this is important
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Turn service knowledge into search-focused content
steps: List specific problems customers search for, rather than writing broad claims such as "we kill bugs."
Ask the operator to explain each problem aloud.
Record and transcribe the explanation, then publish it as a blog post and podcast episode.
Keep publishing regularly; Mike says a podcast should not be abandoned after only a few episodes.

quote.text: it's easier to record and transcribe than it is to write. It's a shorter distance from your brain to your tongue than it is from your brain to your hands.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Build a conversion-focused local landing page
steps: Use a clear headline that names the customer's problem and promises a specific resolution.
Put the headline, short video, social proof and call to action near the top of the page.
Make it easy for a mobile visitor to tap to call or book.
Create specific landing pages for the problems named in ads.

quote.text: Headline, video, social proof, sales letter, and then everything else is if you want to or not.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Use SER-term jingles in skippable local ads
steps: Choose a distinctive search phrase and pair it with a short positioning statement.
Put the phrase and positioning in the opening seconds of the jingle.
Keep the jingle around 15 seconds.
Run the ad in the target local market and let interested viewers continue while skip impressions still deliver the opening phrase.

quote.text: So, frontload it with something that will teach your local market or your worldwide market for that.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Use AI to create and repurpose client content
steps: Have the client provide a spoken explanation or script.
Use Gemini or another chatbot to draft local content from prompts about the service and customer problem.
Use ElevenLabs to clone the client's voice for a read-through when appropriate.
Add the jingle, publish the content and use a transcript as a blog post.

quote.text: I take his script, I clone his voice. Now, he reads it perfectly in any language we want.
quote.speaker: Mike

tactics.name: Use keyword-matched domains and a single booking action
steps: Research what visitors search for in the destination.
Buy an available domain that closely matches the local search phrase.
Build a simple page with one clear booking action.
Use organic search first and add a geographically limited ad budget once the page converts.

quote.text: We created a simple website with one call to action. Book your boat. We send traffic here and they're one tap away from booking our boats.
quote.speaker: Mike

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest describes first-hand businesses, processes, prices and client examples, including a recurring service workflow. Many outcomes are estimates, testimonials or broad claims without supporting records, and some numbers are garbled by the transcript.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Mike promotes his Playmakers AI community and localpresence.com. The host also promotes the podcast, referral offer and submission site. Beehive sponsor read was promotional and has not been treated as a business idea.
